stem: A nurse is discussing cervical cancer screening with an average-risk adult. Which statement best reflects how the screening plan should be determined?

options.A: Use annual cervical cytology after sexual activity begins because frequent testing is the safest approach for average-risk adults.
options.B: Stop screening after one normal adult test when there is no history of cervical disease or immunocompromise.
options.C: Base screening on age, test strategy, prior screening history, and risk factors, with individualized follow-up when risk is higher.
options.D: Select the interval mainly from patient preference because current recommendations do not distinguish among age groups and test strategies.

rationale: The current USPSTF final cervical-cancer screening recommendation uses age and screening-test strategy to determine routine screening and considers prior screening history when deciding whether screening can stop. It also excludes certain higher-risk groups from the routine average-risk recommendation and directs individualized follow-up for them. Therefore C best reflects the framework. A applies unsupported annual screening, B stops screening after a single normal test, and D ignores guideline-based age, test, history, and risk criteria.
educational_objective: Determine cervical cancer screening using the applicable age group, screening strategy, prior screening history, and risk factors rather than a single universal interval.

source_original.stem: A nurse is discussing cervical cancer screening with an average-risk adult. Which statement best reflects how the screening plan should be determined?

options.A: Use annual cervical cytology after sexual activity begins because frequent testing is the safest approach for average-risk adults.
options.B: Stop screening after one normal adult test when there is no history of cervical disease or immunocompromise.
options.C: Base screening on age, test strategy, prior screening history, and risk factors, with individualized follow-up when risk is higher.
options.D: Select the interval mainly from patient preference because current recommendations do not distinguish among age groups and test strategies.

source_original.rationale: The current USPSTF cervical-cancer screening recommendation uses age and screening-test strategy to determine routine intervals and identifies higher-risk situations that require individualized follow-up; prior screening history also affects decisions such as when screening can stop. Option C best reflects that framework. Option A incorrectly applies annual screening to everyone. Option B stops after one normal result without regard to recommended intervals or history. Option D ignores guideline-based age, test, and risk criteria.
source_original.source_detail: USPSTF Cervical Cancer: Screening — current final recommendation framework uses age, test strategy, prior adequate screening and risk status; higher-risk patients require individualized follow-up. USPSTF 2018 Final Recommendation remains the current final recommendation on 2026-08-15; 2024-12-10 draft update remains in-progress and does not supersede the final recommendation. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance; preventive care, screening, prenatal/postpartum and newborn health-promotion activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: No clinical content correction was needed. Currentness was independently rechecked: the 2018 USPSTF statement remains the current final recommendation on 2026-08-16, while the cervical-screening update is still in the finalization/in-progress stage. The item intentionally remains principle-based and avoids unstable interval details.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current USPSTF final recommendation plus USPSTF update-status page.
audit_findings.currentness: 2018 remains the final recommendation; cervical cancer screening is still listed in Recommendations in Progress as checked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Patient Population, Risk, Timing, and Screening Interval sections directly support the planning factors tested.
audit_findings.claim_audit: No unstable age/test interval was asserted in the keyed answer; the item tests the stable framework that screening depends on age, method, history, and risk.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because routine annual cytology is not the USPSTF average-risk strategy and sexual activity does not define the universal start rule.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because one normal test is not sufficient to stop routine screening under the guideline framework.
distractor_audit.C: Correct and captures the decision factors used by USPSTF.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because recommendations explicitly distinguish age groups and test strategies.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C reflects the guideline structure without adding an unsupported universal rule.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are screening-planning statements of comparable length.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Health Promotion and Maintenance through cancer-screening counseling.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second-pass review specifically verified that no newer final USPSTF statement had superseded the cited final recommendation; no unresolved currentness conflict remains.
